decision.summaryForCoordinator: This subject is materially harder to check than its siblings, because it derives twelve named states rather than restating a class list — and every one of them traces to live text. The four platform tuples are enumerated verbatim inside live G14 v1's clean exactByteIntent as '(macos/arm64, macos/x86_64, linux/x86_64, linux/arm64)', and D-002 independently states 'Platforms: macOS (arm64, x86_64) and Linux (x86_64, arm64). Windows deferred.' The four hostile states are == the four kinds in the live hostile exactByteIntent, in the same order. '(TypeScript only)' is quoted from live and every platform-crossed state names TypeScript, corroborated by the live DR-118 row's 'D-002: TypeScript, sole slice-1 role'. Windows occurs zero times, which is the omission that confirms the set was read rather than assumed. Every state also carries a source field naming its origin, which is what made the derivation checkable rather than a judgement call. The SATISFIED handling needed care rather than counting. DR-119 is genuinely SATISFIED in the live register — the only such row in this sequence — so the test that works elsewhere, confirming SATISFIED never appears affirmatively, would give the wrong answer here. Of five occurrences, four are refusals and the fifth reports the live standing: 'DR-119 SATISFIED under D-056 Class B. Closure evidence remains condition 4 / DR-G14 / DR-012 qualification.' That matches D-091, titled 'Record DR-119 SATISFIED under D-056 Class B' and ADOPTED 2026-08-14, and reproduces the live blocker cell exactly. The two prohibitions fail in opposite directions — re-recording versus reopening — and both are refused explicitly. Note also that the subject carries no file08StatusToken, which matters more here than anywhere else in this run: DR-119's status cell IS a SATISFIED record, so importing it would have been the single most damaging available error, and the input-corpus shape removes that route entirely. On numeric thresholds the complete bare-integer set is 1, 4 and 26, and the 4 sits inside 'condition 4 / DR-G14 / DR-012 qualification', matched verbatim against file 08 — a register condition number in a quotation, not a threshold. All seven cited digests match, the three corpus classes are == equal at two carriers plus the register cell, the gate join re-measures with OBL-G14-FX-AUTHORING true as its sole leftover, and the subject did not move. Twenty-five attacks run, twenty-five refuted, zero findings. One thing worth a fixture author's attention: the hostile group is named on the kind axis only, while clean and offline are named per-platform, and the live hostile exactByteIntent says 'per D-002 platform' too — so the full space is sixteen, not four. The artifact is precise about this, calling that group 'four hostile-substitution kinds' rather than cells and quoting the per-platform sentence in the first hostile state's source, so nothing is overstated; the platform crossing simply remains to be named. Disclosure: all three cited claude2 reviews are my own; every claim here was re-derived from live bytes.
